clue.text: Got Sir Andrew to back some thoroughbred

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the run of words are wanted, a stretch sitting inside them
to back up is to go in reverse, so the hidden stretch is read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of Got, all of Sir and the start of Andrew, read backwards

explanation.surface: A knight named Sir Andrew manages to put his money on a racehorse of good breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: An aristo is an aristocrat, a person of noble blood, which is what a thoroughbred is in its figurative sense.

clue.text: On which 8 is found with a German 1 across?

blocks.note: taken as written
1 across is ARISTO; von is the particle marking a German aristocratic name

explanation.surface: A riddle asking where a certain town stands, with a hint about a German noble.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is STRATFORD, the full name of the town being Stratford-upon-Avon.
explanation.definitionFit: The English river flows through Stratford, Shakespeare's birthplace, which sits upon its banks.

clue.text: Man is so narrow-minded

definitions.note: a whole clause: the Isle of Man is insular

blocks.note: first meaning: belonging to an island, as the Isle of Man is
second meaning: inward-looking and parochial

explanation.surface: A sweeping judgement that mankind is intolerant and petty.
explanation.walkthrough: Man here is the Isle of Man, the island in the Irish Sea, not humanity; the capital letter is disguised at the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to an island, and figuratively cut off from outside ideas, hence parochial.

clue.text: "My plays are here!" (No hack poet, as revealed in his troupe)

definitions.text: "My plays are here!" (No hack poet, as revealed in his troupe)

blocks.note: surface: someone proudly pointing out where their work can be seen

blocks.clueFragment: No hack poet, as revealed in his troupe
blocks.note: setter's reading: the great dramatist of 5 speaking of the national troupe of actors that bears his name

explanation.surface: A boastful playwright announces his plays are on, with an aside that he is no hack and his actors prove it.
explanation.walkthrough: The full answer is THE ROYAL SHAKESPEARE COMPANY: these two lights hold THE ROYAL and COMPANY, with 5 down supplying the poet's name between them.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Stratford-based theatre troupe devoted to staging the works of the Bard, so his dramas are performed there.

clue.text: Mass introduction when work unit enters drill square

indicators.note: something that enters goes inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: as in 'as I left' meaning at the time that
physical education, school drill
the erg is a unit of work in physics
S is an abbreviation used for square

explanation.surface: Soldiers going to Mass march onto the parade ground as part of the day's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Drill square looks like a parade ground; split it into drill and square.
explanation.definitionFit: The Asperges is the sprinkling of holy water with which the principal Sunday Mass opens in the Catholic rite.

clue.text: 8 on 1 down's raison d'etre?

blocks.note: surface: a question about why a town exists at all
setter's reading: Stratford-upon-Avon is famous, and lives off tourism, because of the playwright born there

explanation.surface: A question about why the town of 8 on the river 1 down exists.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is STRATFORD and 1 down is AVON, so the subject is Stratford-upon-Avon.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is world-famous as the birthplace of England's greatest dramatist, whose memory sustains its tourist trade.

clue.text: 9 Greek pieces in French and English translation

indicators.note: translating turns words into another form, so these letters are rendered in a new order

blocks.note: en is French for in
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Nine pieces of Greek writing, available in French and English versions.
explanation.walkthrough: The Enneads are Plotinus's writings, gathered into six sets of nine treatises.
explanation.definitionFit: An ennead is a group of nine, the name given to each of the nine-part divisions of Plotinus's Greek philosophy.

clue.text: G-Gibraltar rejecting the Spanish tourist

indicators.note: rejecting something throws it back, so the Spanish word is turned round

blocks.note: the stammered initial, taken as written
Gibraltar is known as the Rock
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A stammering local in Gibraltar turns away a Spanish visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter G-G supplies a separate letter G before Gibraltar. Grockle is West Country English slang, mainly Devon and Cornwall, for a holidaymaker.
explanation.definitionFit: In the dialect of south-west England, a grockle is a disparaging word for a visiting holidaymaker.

clue.text: Doctor of fallen women elevated on 1 down

definitions.note: the town known as being on the river at 1 down

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting the words up means reading them from bottom to top

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for doctor
taken as written
a dated term for women of loose morals

explanation.surface: A physician who rescues fallen women has been raised to a position in some town.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase doctor of fallen women is turned upside down, not just one part.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratford is the Warwickshire market town standing on the Avon, its full name being Stratford-upon-Avon.

clue.text: Native aphrodisiac?

blocks.note: first meaning: a native is a British-bred ..., such as those from Whitstable
second meaning: a food reputed to stir desire

explanation.walkthrough: Native looks like an adjective, but it is a shellfish dealer's noun for a home-grown oyster.
explanation.definitionFit: The shellfish famously has a reputation for stimulating romance, and a cultivated British one is called a native.

clue.text: One can't miss this farm entrance

blocks.note: first meaning: the proverbially huge target that even a poor shot will hit
second meaning: the big gate into an agricultural building

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom says a bad marksman couldn't hit one, so it stands for any target impossible to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: It is literally the large door of a farmyard building, and figuratively a target so big nobody misses.

clue.text: Oversupply with little time for lake method, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps marks the words as one possible arrangement of letters that could be rearranged otherwise

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written

explanation.surface: A business that has too much stock and too little time to try out a method involving a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' reads like a substitution signal, T for L, but it is simply part of the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To flood the market is the idiom for selling so much of a product that supply exceeds demand.

clue.text: Parasite killer's attempt on father: I'd say the game's up!

indicators.note: what I would say is what is spoken, so the phrase is wanted for how it is heard

blocks.note: a try is an attempt
pa is an informal word for father
no side is the call that ends a rugby match

explanation.surface: Someone's try against their dad ends with the declaration that the game is over.
explanation.walkthrough: No side is the referee's term for full time in rugby, which also fits try in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A trypanocide is a drug that kills trypanosomes, the protozoan parasites behind sleeping sickness.

clue.text: With two sovereigns to pay back, 'e's made Primate of the Rock

indicators.note: back means returning in the other direction, so pay is read the wrong way round

blocks.note: Babar, king of the elephants, with R for rex (king) inside him
taken as written
he with the H dropped, as written

explanation.surface: A Cockney who owes two gold sovereigns finds himself appointed archbishop of Gibraltar.
explanation.walkthrough: Primate looks ecclesiastical, but it is the animal; the Rock is Gibraltar, where these tailless macaques famously live.
explanation.definitionFit: The Barbary ape is the macaque monkey living wild on Gibraltar, the only wild primate population in Europe.

clue.text: Guarantors lean toward eccentrics

blocks.note: an aircraft banks when it tilts in a turn
a card is an amusing oddball

explanation.surface: People who vouch for others tend to favour oddballs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheque guarantee cards issued by banks assured shops that a customer's cheque would be honoured.

clue.text: Where marriages end in mere nothings

indicators.note: in says the wanted letters lie inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the end of mere and start of nothings

explanation.surface: A cynical remark that weddings finish up as nothing much at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nevada city was long famous for quick, easy divorces, so many marriages were dissolved there.

clue.text: My Lord! He brewed mead!

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients together, so these letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A servant's astonished exclamation that his master has made his own honey wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydromel is a drink of honey and water, which when fermented is the same as the honey wine.

clue.text: Des Anglais promenade here when it's fine

blocks.note: first meaning: the city whose seafront is the Promenade des Anglais
second meaning: pleasant, agreeable

explanation.surface: The English take a stroll along the front when the weather is good.
explanation.walkthrough: Read in French, des Anglais promenade looks like English people walking, but it names the famous seafront boulevard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riviera resort has the Promenade des Anglais, and the English adjective means pleasant or agreeable.

clue.text: See 3
Informer and offspring brought before the beak!

blocks.note: a canary is underworld slang for someone who sings to the police
seed in the biblical sense of descendants

explanation.surface: A police informant and his son are hauled up before a magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: The beak is British slang for a magistrate, but here it is a bird's bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdseed for caged songbirds is set in front of a bird's bill to be pecked at and eaten.

clue.text: Not a sound out of it

definitions.text: Not a sound out of it

blocks.clueFragment: Not a sound out of it
blocks.note: surface: something keeping completely silent
setter's reading: beyond the range of hearing, where no sound can reach you

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone or something is totally silent.
explanation.definitionFit: When you are beyond the distance within which noises carry, you can hear nothing at all.

clue.text: Slow passage from a soldier in difficulty

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

blocks.note: ado is fuss or trouble
A plus GI, an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier in a tight spot makes slow progress through a narrow corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: An adagio is a movement or section of music played at a slow, leisurely tempo.

clue.text: 5's work of sorcery from ode composition

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters are assembled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A play by the dramatist of 5 is a piece of magic conjured from a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 is SHAKESPEARE, so his work is one of his plays.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of one of the Bard's early farces, about two sets of twins mistaken for each other.

clue.text: Cracked peal from Calliope leaves her sister standing

indicators.note: a cracked bell rings jumbled, so the letters of the word are scrambled
the letters leave, departing from the name and taking themselves away

blocks.note: the Muse of epic poetry
taken as written; its letters come out of the Muse's name in a different order

explanation.surface: A cracked bell ringing out from a steam organ leaves a sister standing still.
explanation.walkthrough: A calliope is also a steam organ, which suits the peal in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Clio, the Muse of history, is one of the nine daughters of Zeus and Mnemosyne, so a sister to the Muse of epic poetry.

clue.text: The way strength of character is an aid to winter driving

blocks.note: a road is a way
grit is courage and resolve

explanation.surface: Determination is the secret of getting about when the weather turns icy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gritting lorries spread coarse sand and salt on icy highways to give tyres purchase in frost and snow.

clue.text: I'm Prince Henry: where's the battle?

blocks.note: taken as written
P is the abbreviation for prince
Hal is the nickname of the young Henry V in Shakespeare's plays

explanation.surface: Young Prince Hal, before Agincourt, asks where the fighting is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian city in Manipur was the site of a decisive 1944 engagement in which Allied forces turned back the Japanese invasion.

clue.text: Spot cash for Alec Leamas?

blocks.note: to spy is to spot
a synonym

explanation.surface: Ready money paid out to a fictional British agent.
explanation.walkthrough: Alec Leamas is the agent in John le Carré's The Spy Who Came in from the Cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Funds paid to or by an intelligence agent for espionage work, as would go to le Carré's agent.

clue.text: Lit up? B-bingo!

blocks.note: the stammered initial, taken as written
lotto is a game like bingo

explanation.surface: A thrilled cry of a winner who stammers out the call at a bingo hall.
explanation.walkthrough: Lit up looks like illuminated, but it is slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions are slang for heavily intoxicated: someone lit up is as drunk as someone blotto.
